next_step: Finalize committed GPU hours, sign SOW draft, schedule legal review
notes:
Background: Mid-market product analytics SaaS (B2B). Engineering-led buying group (CTO + Head of Platform) with product manager as day-to-day sponsor. Started with hosted API eval for embeddings/doc-search in Q4; moved to a short Dedicated POC for latency and cost predictability.

POC summary: 2-week Dedicated pilot (single GX100-equivalent pool) completed 2026-02-28. Workloads: embedding index + real-time reranking + conversational support assistant. Measured: median gen latency 85ms (token stream), 95th pct 210ms; throughput ~120 reqs/min sustained per instance during peak simulation. Observations: prefix caching reduced token spend by ~18% for support flows.

Pricing/packaging discussion highlights: negotiating committed GPU-hour tiers (monthly commit target 1.5k GPU-hours for initial 6-month ramp). Interested in burst capacity for seasonal spikes (up to 3x commit) and clear overage rules: prefer per-GPU-hour over per-token for predictability. Asking for ramp schedule (month 1 commit at 50%, month 2 at 75%, month 3 full) and a 10% discount escalator tied to usage thresholds. Concern about price shock on overage during onboarding.

Security/compliance: require SSO (SAML) + enterprise audit logs; KMS integration for model keys; want retention controls and option for EU data residency for parts of customer data. Completed initial security questionnaire; waiting on SOC2 Type II evidence and encryption-in-transit proof.

Commercial: internal stakeholders pushed for a conservative ARR commit. Legal requested SOW with explicit overage caps and termination rights if performance SLAs not met for three consecutive sprints. Finance asked for 60-day net terms — Redwood pricing team flagged as non-standard.

Recent activity/timeline: see timeline field for discrete items.

Direct quote from CTO on 2026-03-04 demo call: "We like the latency profile and the caching gains — but we need comfort on committed economics and a guardrail for bursts."

Next steps (short): Redwood to provide revised SOW with 3-tier commit options, explicit burst pricing and an overage ceiling; attach SOC2 evidence link; schedule procurement call w/ legal (2026-03-18 proposed).
